correctness.rationale: For the real finite unit-edge graph Banach sum norm, every boundary vertex lifts uniquely to a vertex of Q. The tight-edge graph must anchor every component; if no component has opposite-sign anchors, a two-sided b-variation contradicts extremality. The opposite signs force 2(1-b)=kb and k<=diameter, all vertices lie on the parity lattice. Truncated distance functions attain each k, as witnessed by full-rank active anchors and tight geodesics. The dual grid maximum follows from convex polytope extreme-point representation and feasibility; path DP obeys prefix induction. Current CHECKER.py independently finds 106 boundary vertices over seven graphs and verifies 126 exact norm comparisons plus 60 path DP comparisons. Finite tests do not replace unrestricted proof.

value.rationale: The problem is motivated by 2023 bounded-Lipschitz extreme-point work and 2022 finite metric Dudley computation. The answer proves a complete attainable integer slope spectrum for every finite unit graph; this is a natural metric-combinatorial classification with direct exact signed-measure dual formula and transparent cubic-time dynamic programming on paths. It is not an arbitrary tiny finite datum, nor a merely relabeled generic LP.
